findings.description: `githubRefs` discards a foreign repository reference and records it only with `console.error`, without retaining it for the frontier report. When an issue cites a foreign blocker or parent, the JSON backlog contains neither that edge nor an explanation for its removal, and the dashboard reads that JSON rather than stderr.
findings.title: The dashboard hides dropped blockers

evidence.explanation: The new branch drops the reference after writing to stderr. Ticket construction receives only the surviving numbers, while the report and dashboard view have no field for ignored references.

findings.description: The added test calls `parseProseBlockers` and `parseParent` directly but never runs `triage-apply` with a foreign repository reference. That leaves the new repository initialization in the triage command untested, even though this command reads and simulates its own census without calling `frontierTracker()`.
findings.title: Triage's new path lacks command coverage

evidence.explanation: The changed command explicitly initializes repository state before its census and simulation. The new tests verify only direct parser calls; the separate triage test file has a CLI harness but no cross-repository case.
